segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. WHATWG/browser-standard timer APIs.

notes: The handle is Node's `Timeout` object (its `lib/internal/timers.js` ported to TypeScript, [ADR-01411](../adr/ADR-01411.md)): `ref`/`unref`/`hasRef`/`refresh`/`close`, `+timeout` as its id, which `clearTimeout` also takes
Bare global functions, matching real JS (not a namespace)

The delay is clamped to `[1, 2^31-1]` ms as Node does — an omitted, `0`, negative or oversized delay is 1 ms, so a chain of zero-delay timers advances one millisecond per link (`setInterval` too; `setImmediate` is not clamped) ([ADR-01071](../adr/ADR-01071.md))
An active interval that's never cleared keeps the process running indefinitely, matching real Node

Runs in the loop's check phase, after I/O polling, as in Node: scheduled from an I/O callback it runs before a 0 ms `setTimeout`; the handle is Node's `Immediate` object ([ADR-01411](../adr/ADR-01411.md))
A real microtask FIFO distinct from the timer queue, drained after the synchronous script and before timers ([TDD-00083](../tdd/TDD-00083.md) Stage 3)

Node's lib/timers/promises.js in TypeScript: promise timers that resolve with their value, `setInterval` as an async iterator, an `AbortSignal` rejecting with `AbortError`, `ref: false`, and Node's option validation ([ADR-01271](../adr/ADR-01271.md))
